subject.title: fix(repair): publish only validated target commits

question: Should repair execution intentionally require this Linux namespace, capability-drop, read-only-mount, and Landlock ABI 3 boundary before authenticated publication?
rationale: Automation can verify mechanics but cannot decide whether the reduced runner compatibility and fail-closed availability behavior are the repository's intended permanent trust boundary.

options.title: Accept after current-head proof
options.body: Retain the proposed fail-closed Linux boundary and merge only after repeating filesystem, network, descendant-reaping, dependency-install, and immutable-publication proof on the exact current head.

options.title: Split immutable publication first
options.body: Land the validated-commit and isolated-Git publication changes separately, then review the broader execution-containment and package-manager policy in a follow-up PR.

options.title: Preserve broader runner support
options.body: Pause this design and define a compatible fallback or separately configured strict mode instead of making the new Linux boundary unconditional.

recommendation.title: Accept after current-head proof
recommendation.body: Retain the proposed fail-closed Linux boundary and merge only after repeating filesystem, network, descendant-reaping, dependency-install, and immutable-publication proof on the exact current head.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied PR and predecessor history show the strongest ownership of the affected repair validation and publication architecture.
